exposure: Delivery before or at estimated due date vs. delivery after estimated due date
cohort: 827 women who presented for an intended vaginal breech delivery of a singleton at a perinatal center between January 2010 and December 2016
finding: There was no significant difference in maternal and neonatal short-term mortality and morbidity between women who delivered before or at their estimated due date and those who delivered after their estimated due date.
mod_finding: The rate of caesarian sections and delivery maneuvers was higher in the group of patients who delivered later than 40 1/7 weeks of gestation.
